topic.title: Reward Representations and Preference-Based Policy Learning
topic.overview: This topic asks how rewards should be represented, inferred, or supplied to learning agents. Papers explore intrinsic rewards, reward machines, successor-style representations, inverse reinforcement learning, and preference-based optimization. A representative forward-backward representation learns long-range state–action relationships without rewards, then converts a newly specified reward into a policy without additional planning.
topic.whyItMatters: An agent's behavior depends on both its learning algorithm and the way its objective is expressed. Reusable dynamics representations can support many tasks, while learned reward models introduce capacity and statistical assumptions that affect which preferences the final policy can satisfy.
topic.evolution: The representatives range from learning utilities and macro-actions to reward-free behavior spaces and episodic feedback. Recent preference-learning theory compares explicit reward modeling with direct policy optimization, showing that relative performance depends on model misspecification and available samples.
openQuestions: Which reward representations support useful adaptation to genuinely new tasks?
How should reward-model and policy capacity be matched when learning from limited preferences?

papers.tldr: Reward machines that call other reward machines enable faster task learning and make some otherwise infeasible reward representations learnable.

papers.title: Identifiability and Generalizability in Constrained Inverse Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: Constraints and regularization change which rewards can be identified, and guaranteed transfer requires recovering the true reward up to a constant.

papers.title: Internally Rewarded Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: A clipped linear reward reduces reward-noise effects and improves training when a policy and its reward-generating discriminator learn together.

papers.title: Invariance in Policy Optimisation and Partial Identifiability in Reward Learning
papers.tldr: An invariance-based framework characterizes reward ambiguity and connects what reward-learning data identifies to what downstream tasks need.

papers.title: Principled Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback from Pairwise or K-wise Comparisons
papers.tldr: For linear rewards, comparison-based reward estimates can converge while policy learning still requires pessimism and sufficient coverage for good performance.

papers.title: Provable Reset-free Reinforcement Learning by No-Regret Reduction
papers.tldr: A two-player-game reduction yields conditional guarantees for learning good policies while making resets increasingly infrequent.

papers.title: Reachability-Aware Laplacian Representation in Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: Rescaling Laplacian representation dimensions better aligns distances with state reachability, improving reward shaping and bottleneck discovery in the reported results.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning Can Be More Efficient with Multiple Rewards
papers.tldr: Multiple rewards can improve action-elimination regret bounds when they share an optimal policy, with a separate bandit guarantee when rewards disagree.

papers.title: Settling the Reward Hypothesis
papers.tldr: The paper aims to settle the reward hypothesis by specifying the requirements under which goals can be represented as expected cumulative reward maximisation.

papers.title: TGRL: An Algorithm for Teacher Guided Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: TGRL dynamically balances teacher imitation and reward-based learning, outperforming strong baselines across the reported domains without hyperparameter tuning.

papers.title: Towards Theoretical Understanding of Inverse Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: For finite-horizon IRL with a generative model, uniform sampling estimates compatible reward sets with sample complexity matching a minimax lower bound up to logarithmic factors.

papers.title: A Definition of Continual Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: The paper defines continual reinforcement learning as settings where all best-performing agents must keep learning indefinitely.

papers.title: A State Representation for Diminishing Rewards
papers.tldr: The λ representation extends successor representations to evaluate policies when repeated rewards have diminishing value.

papers.title: Connected Superlevel Set in (Deep) Reinforcement Learning and its Application to Minimax Theorems
papers.tldr: Connected policy-objective superlevel sets and a stronger equiconnectedness property yield minimax guarantees for a class of robust reinforcement learning problems.

papers.title: Contrastive Retrospection: honing in on critical steps for rapid learning and generalization in RL
papers.tldr: ConSpec learns prototypes of critical past states and rewards their recurrence to improve reinforcement-learning credit assignment and generalization.

papers.title: Distributional Pareto-Optimal Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: DPMORL learns policies that balance competing objectives using preferences over return distributions, including uncertainty beyond average outcomes.

papers.title: Distributional Policy Evaluation: a Maximum Entropy approach to Representation Learning
papers.tldr: A maximum entropy framework guides policy evaluation toward state representations that balance information preservation and estimation complexity.

papers.title: Diversify \& Conquer: Outcome-directed Curriculum RL via Out-of-Distribution Disagreement
papers.tldr: D2C turns classifier disagreement and a few desired-outcome examples into intermediate goals for reinforcement learning exploration.

papers.title: Doubly Robust Augmented Transfer for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: DRaT transfers experience across sparse-reward tasks while accounting for differences in both rewards and dynamics through theoretically grounded value estimation.

papers.title: Interpretable Reward Redistribution in Reinforcement Learning: A Causal Approach
papers.tldr: Generative Return Decomposition uses causal models to explain delayed rewards and construct compact representations for policy learning while preserving policy invariance.

papers.title: Inverse Preference Learning: Preference-based RL without a Reward Function
papers.tldr: Inverse Preference Learning uses the reward information encoded in a Q-function to learn from offline preferences without a separate reward model.

papers.title: Inverse Reinforcement Learning with the Average Reward Criterion
papers.tldr: Average-reward inverse reinforcement learning recovers policies and rewards without a known expert discount factor, using algorithms with proven complexity bounds.

papers.title: Is RLHF More Difficult than Standard RL? A Theoretical Perspective
papers.tldr: For broad classes of preference models, theoretical reductions solve preference-based reinforcement learning using reward-based methods with small or no extra costs.

papers.title: Pitfall of Optimism: Distributional Reinforcement Learning by Randomizing Risk Criterion
papers.tldr: Randomizing action-selection risk criteria supports exploration while preserving a risk-neutral objective, with convergence guarantees and empirical gains.

papers.title: Prioritizing Samples in Reinforcement Learning with Reducible Loss
papers.tldr: Prioritizing replay samples whose losses steadily decrease improves robustness over random sampling and loss-based prioritization in the reported experiments.

papers.title: Robust Knowledge Transfer in Tiered Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: Under Optimal Value Dominance, tiered learning can gain state-dependent transfer benefits while retaining near-optimal regret when tasks are dissimilar.

papers.title: Sequential Preference Ranking for Efficient Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.tldr: SeqRank organizes sequential trajectory comparisons into preference rankings to extract more learning value from human feedback.

papers.title: Would I have gotten that reward? Long-term credit assignment by counterfactual contribution analysis
papers.tldr: COCOA assigns credit through counterfactual contributions to rewards, reducing gradient bias and variance in long-term credit-assignment experiments.

papers.title: A Distributional Analogue to the Successor Representation
papers.tldr: A distributional successor measure separates transition structure from rewards and enables zero-shot, risk-sensitive policy evaluation.

papers.title: A Minimaximalist Approach to Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.tldr: SPO uses self-comparisons to train policies without a separate reward model, with guarantees covering complex preferences and encouraging continuous-control results.

papers.title: A Unified Linear Programming Framework for Offline Reward Learning from Human Demonstrations and Feedback
papers.tldr: A linear programming framework learns feasible reward functions from offline demonstrations and feedback with optimality and sample-efficiency guarantees.

papers.title: An Information Theoretic Approach to Interaction-Grounded Learning
papers.tldr: VI-IGL learns hidden rewards through an information-based objective that enforces the conditional-independence structure assumed in interaction-grounded learning.

papers.title: EvoRainbow: Combining Improvements in Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning for Policy Search
papers.tldr: EvoRainbow combines empirically effective evolutionary and reinforcement-learning mechanisms to improve policy search across varied tasks.

papers.title: Exploration-Driven Policy Optimization in RLHF: Theoretical Insights on Efficient Data Utilization
papers.tldr: The paper gives low-query performance bounds for policy-based RLHF that learns rewards from comparisons between trajectories.

papers.title: Global Reinforcement Learning : Beyond Linear and Convex Rewards via Submodular Semi-gradient Methods
papers.tldr: Global RL models interactions across trajectories and solves the resulting objectives through sequences of standard RL problems with curvature-dependent approximation guarantees.

papers.title: How Does Goal Relabeling Improve Sample Efficiency?
papers.tldr: The paper explains goal relabeling through improved hypothesis elimination and develops GOALIVE with a complexity measure offering best-case exponential improvement.

papers.title: Offline Inverse RL: New Solution Concepts and Provably Efficient Algorithms
papers.tldr: The paper formalizes feasible reward sets for offline inverse reinforcement learning and introduces two provably efficient estimation algorithms.

papers.title: PIPER: Primitive-Informed Preference-based Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning via Hindsight Relabeling
papers.tldr: PIPER uses primitive-generated preferences, reward relabeling, and feasible-subgoal regularization to improve hierarchical learning in sparse-reward robotic tasks.

papers.title: Principled Penalty-based Methods for Bilevel Reinforcement Learning and RLHF
papers.tldr: A penalty-based framework brings theoretical analysis and gradient algorithms to bilevel reinforcement learning, with demonstrations in games and RLHF.

papers.title: Provable Interactive Learning with Hindsight Instruction Feedback
papers.tldr: Under a low-rank instruction–response model, LORIL learns from hindsight instructions with regret depending on intrinsic rank rather than response-space size.

papers.title: Reward Model Learning vs. Direct Policy Optimization: A Comparative Analysis of Learning from Human Preferences
papers.tldr: Within specified policy and reward classes, the paper compares RLHF and DPO across statistical error, optimization, and reward misspecification.

papers.title: Reward Shaping for Reinforcement Learning with An Assistant Reward Agent
papers.tldr: A learned reward agent supplies auxiliary feedback that helps a policy agent learn from sparse and delayed rewards.

papers.title: RIME: Robust Preference-based Reinforcement Learning with Noisy Preferences
papers.tldr: RIME combines dynamic preference filtering with a warm-started reward model to improve robustness to noisy human feedback.

papers.title: RL-CFR: Improving Action Abstraction for Imperfect Information Extensive-Form Games with Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: RL-CFR learns dynamic action abstractions that improve poker performance without increasing counterfactual regret minimization solving time.

papers.title: To the Max: Reinventing Reward in Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: Max-reward reinforcement learning optimizes the highest reward instead of cumulative reward and shows benefits in two evaluated goal-reaching environments.

papers.title: A theoretical case-study of Scalable Oversight in Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: This theoretical study shows how hierarchical reinforcement learning can use size-limited human feedback, with different requirements for numerical and comparative judgments.

papers.title: Action Gaps and Advantages in Continuous-Time Distributional Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: The paper explains why distributional reinforcement learning struggles at high decision frequencies and introduces a superiority-based algorithm that improves simulated controllers.

papers.title: An Analytical Study of Utility Functions in Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes preferences and utility functions for multi-objective reinforcement learning that guarantee an optimal policy exists.

papers.title: Catastrophic Goodhart: regularizing RLHF with KL divergence does not mitigate heavy-tailed reward misspecification
papers.tldr: KL regularization can fail to prevent arbitrarily inflated reward without utility gains when reward errors are heavy-tailed.

papers.title: Contextual Bilevel Reinforcement Learning for Incentive Alignment
papers.tldr: CB-RL learns incentives from followers’ observed behavior while accounting for random context and allowing unknown follower training procedures.

papers.title: Distributional Reinforcement Learning with Regularized Wasserstein Loss
papers.tldr: SinkhornDRL uses a regularized Wasserstein loss to learn return distributions, with contraction guarantees and strong Atari results.

papers.title: Distributional Successor Features Enable Zero-Shot Policy Optimization
papers.tldr: DiSPO models distributions of long-term outcomes and corresponding behaviors to enable zero-shot policy optimization across reward functions.

papers.title: Foundations of Multivariate Distributional Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: The paper provides tractable, provably convergent algorithms for learning return distributions with multidimensional rewards.

papers.title: Goal-Conditioned On-Policy Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: GCPO combines demonstration pretraining and an adaptive goal curriculum to learn tasks with both immediate-state and history-dependent rewards.

papers.title: Going Beyond Heuristics by Imposing Policy Improvement as a Constraint
papers.tldr: The method uses a policy-improvement constraint to turn heuristic guidance into better task performance in finite-data reinforcement learning.

papers.title: In-Trajectory Inverse Reinforcement Learning: Learn Incrementally Before an Ongoing Trajectory Terminates
papers.tldr: In-trajectory inverse reinforcement learning updates rewards and policies before a demonstration finishes.

papers.title: Learning the Optimal Policy for Balancing Short-Term and Long-Term Rewards
papers.tldr: DPPL decomposes multi-reward policy learning and interprets preference choices through minimum acceptable reward thresholds.

papers.title: Measuring Goal-Directedness
papers.tldr: MEG formalizes goal-directedness in causal models and Markov decision processes, with theoretical properties and algorithms demonstrated in small-scale experiments.

papers.title: Near-Minimax-Optimal Distributional Reinforcement Learning with a Generative Model
papers.tldr: A new model-based distributional RL algorithm achieves minimax-optimal return-distribution approximation up to logarithmic factors in the generative model regime.

papers.title: Online Iterative Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with General Preference Model
papers.tldr: A preference-game formulation broadens RLHF beyond reward-based assumptions and supports sample-efficient offline and online learning algorithms.

papers.title: Provable Partially Observable Reinforcement Learning with Privileged Information
papers.tldr: The paper establishes conditional efficiency guarantees for practical partially observable reinforcement-learning methods that use privileged information during training.

papers.title: Randomized algorithms and PAC bounds for inverse reinforcement learning in continuous spaces
papers.tldr: The paper develops randomized methods and probabilistic error guarantees for inferring costs from optimal behavior in continuous state and action spaces.

papers.title: REBEL: Reinforcement Learning via Regressing Relative Rewards
papers.tldr: REBEL reduces policy optimization to regression on relative rewards, offering theoretical guarantees and competitive generative-model results with a simpler implementation.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning Under Latent Dynamics: Toward Statistical and Algorithmic Modularity
papers.tldr: The paper identifies tractability barriers and sufficient conditions for latent-dynamics RL, plus efficient reductions in two specified settings.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning with LTL and $\omega$-Regular Objectives via Optimality-Preserving Translation to Average Rewards
papers.tldr: An optimality-preserving translation to average rewards establishes asymptotic learning of optimal policies for temporal-logic and omega-regular objectives.

papers.title: Reward Machines for Deep RL in Noisy and Uncertain Environments
papers.tldr: The paper develops reinforcement learning algorithms that use Reward Machine task structure when observations and task-event interpretations are uncertain.

papers.title: Sub-optimal Experts mitigate Ambiguity in Inverse Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: Adding sub-optimal experts can narrow the reward functions compatible with optimal demonstrations and improve identifiability in inverse reinforcement learning.

papers.title: The Value of Reward Lookahead in Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: The paper derives worst-case reward ratios quantifying the advantage of observing some or all future rewards before acting.

papers.title: Towards the Transferability of Rewards Recovered via Regularized Inverse Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: The paper establishes sufficient conditions for rewards learned from demonstrations to transfer across dynamics, using principal angles to characterize transition-law differences.

papers.title: When Your AIs Deceive You: Challenges of Partial Observability in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.tldr: When human evaluators see only part of an interaction, RLHF can provably encourage misleading behavior under specified conditions.

papers.title: Can RLHF be More Efficient with Imperfect Reward Models? A Policy Coverage Perspective
papers.tldr: The paper develops theory and a practical selection strategy for using imperfect reward models to accelerate online RLHF.

papers.title: Decoding Rewards in Competitive Games: Inverse Game Theory with Entropy Regularization
papers.tldr: A framework recovers competitive players’ reward functions under linear assumptions while using confidence sets to represent plausible alternatives.

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Hierarchical Preference Design
papers.tldr: HERON turns hierarchically ranked feedback into trajectory preferences and learned rewards, improving agent learning in the evaluated applications.

papers.title: Improving the Continuity of Goal-Achievement Ability via Policy Self-Regularization for Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: Margin-based policy self-regularization improves success across neighboring goals by controlling how much their policies differ.

papers.title: Intersectional Fairness in Reinforcement Learning with Large State and Constraint Spaces
papers.tldr: The paper provides oracle-efficient reinforcement-learning algorithms for possibly exponentially many intersecting-group objectives, with structural conditions for large state spaces.

papers.title: Learning Utilities from Demonstrations in Markov Decision Processes
papers.tldr: A risk-sensitive behavioral model and two efficient algorithms learn utility functions from demonstrations while characterizing their partial identifiability.

papers.title: Multi-objective Linear Reinforcement Learning with Lexicographic Rewards
papers.tldr: The paper gives per-objective regret guarantees for linear reinforcement learning with hierarchically ordered rewards, including a misspecified setting.

papers.title: Of Mice and Machines: A Comparison of Learning Between Real World Mice and RL Agents
papers.tldr: A mouse–RL comparison reveals excessive risk-taking by agents, and two proposed mechanisms produce more mouse-like caution and predator avoidance.

papers.title: Policy Filtration for RLHF to Mitigate Noise in Reward Models
papers.tldr: PF-PPO filters potentially unreliable reward feedback, improving code generation and mathematical reasoning in the reported experiments.

papers.title: Policy-labeled Preference Learning: Is Preference Enough for RLHF?
papers.tldr: PPL models preferences through policy regret to correct likelihood mismatches and improve feedback-based learning in continuous control.

papers.title: Proto Successor Measure: Representing the Behavior Space of an RL Agent
papers.tldr: Proto Successor Measure represents behaviors with shared basis functions, enabling near-optimal reward-specific policies without further environment interaction.

papers.title: Reward Translation via Reward Machine in Semi-Alignable MDPs
papers.tldr: Neural reward translation matches reward machines to transfer rewards between environments that permit only partial alignment.

papers.title: The Perils of Optimizing Learned Reward Functions: Low Training Error Does Not Guarantee Low Regret
papers.tldr: Low reward-model test error can coexist with high policy regret because optimization shifts distributions, even when policy regularization is used.

papers.title: Towards Theoretical Understanding of Sequential Decision Making with Preference Feedback
papers.tldr: The paper formalizes links between partial preferences, utilities, and rewards, including computational barriers and an efficient reward-approximation method.

papers.title: Unraveling the Interplay between Carryover Effects and Reward Autocorrelations in Switchback Experiments
papers.tldr: Switchback design effectiveness depends on carryover and reward-error autocorrelation, with findings that hold across the reinforcement-learning estimators analyzed.

papers.title: Beyond Scalar Rewards: An Axiomatic Framework for Lexicographic MDPs
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes when ordered priorities require vector rewards and shows that their optimal policies preserve useful scalar-reward properties.

papers.title: Constructing an Optimal Behavior Basis for the Option Keyboard
papers.tldr: An efficiently constructed behavior basis lets the Option Keyboard solve new linear tasks optimally and extends optimality to certain nonlinear tasks.

papers.title: Convergence Theorems for Entropy-Regularized and Distributional Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: A theoretical framework selects an interpretable optimal policy while ensuring convergence of its values and return distributions.

papers.title: Information-Theoretic Reward Decomposition for Generalizable RLHF
papers.tldr: This method separates response-only and prompt-dependent rewards, then uses the decomposition to improve reward learning and generalization.

papers.title: Iterative Foundation Model Fine-Tuning on Multiple Rewards
papers.tldr: An iterative reinforcement learning method fine-tunes foundation models across multiple rewards, with theoretical analysis and evaluations in text and molecular generation.

papers.title: On Feasible Rewards in Multi-Agent Inverse Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes rewards compatible with multi-agent equilibria and analyzes learning in an entropy-regularized setting with a unique equilibrium.

papers.title: Optimal Dynamic Regret by Transformers for Non-Stationary Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: The paper proves that transformers can learn strategies with nearly optimal dynamic regret in non-stationary reinforcement learning and reports competitive experiments.

papers.title: Preference Learning with Response Time: Robust Losses and Guarantees
papers.tldr: Under a drift-diffusion model of decisions, adding response times to preference choices improves reward-learning rates and receives support from image-preference experiments.

papers.title: Reinforcement learning for one-shot DAG scheduling with comparability identification and dense reward
papers.tldr: Removing redundant priority comparisons and providing dense node-level rewards improves learned one-shot DAG scheduling in experiments.

papers.title: Reward-Aware Proto-Representations in Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: The paper develops learning methods and theory for reward-aware default representations, finding benefits over successor representations in several reinforcement learning settings.

papers.title: Reward-oriented Causal Representation Learning
papers.tldr: Reward-oriented causal learning recovers only the hidden structure needed to choose good interventions, with regret guarantees for linear models.

papers.title: STAIR: Addressing Stage Misalignment through Temporal-Aligned Preference Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: STAIR improves preference-based learning by identifying task stages and prioritizing comparisons between behavior segments from the same stage.

papers.title: STAR: Efficient Preference-based Reinforcement Learning via Dual Regularization
papers.tldr: STAR improves preference-based reinforcement learning by jointly limiting reward-model overfitting and overly optimistic policy value estimates.

papers.title: Strategyproof Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.tldr: The paper proves a strategyproofness–welfare tradeoff in RLHF and proposes an approximately strategyproof algorithm with conditional convergence guarantees.

papers.title: Trust Region Reward Optimization and Proximal Inverse Reward Optimization Algorithm
papers.tldr: TRRO guarantees improving expert-behavior likelihood, and its practical PIRO algorithm achieves strong reward recovery and imitation results.

papers.title: When Can Model-Free Reinforcement Learning be Enough for Thinking?
papers.tldr: Thought MDPs explain how initialization can enable model-free reinforcement learning to learn internal actions that improve subsequent decisions.

papers.title: Compositional Behavioral Semantics for State Abstraction in Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: A unified theoretical framework explains how behavioral properties and metrics can be defined and safely transferred under reinforcement learning state abstraction.

papers.title: Expected Return Causes Outcome-Level Mode Collapse in Reinforcement Learning and How to Fix It with Inverse Probability Scaling
papers.tldr: Inverse probability scaling counters expected-return-driven outcome collapse and improves diversity in tested reasoning and molecular generation tasks.

papers.title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Sparse-Reward Search in Commutative Algebra
papers.tldr: An options-based hierarchical reinforcement-learning method improves sparse-reward graph search for counterexamples related to Kalai’s algebraic Hirsch conjecture.

papers.title: MAVRL: Learning Reward Functions from Multiple Feedback Types with Amortized Variational Inference
papers.tldr: MAVRL combines heterogeneous feedback through Bayesian reward inference, improving learned policies while exposing uncertainty and cross-feedback consistency.

papers.title: Maximum Likelihood Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: MaxRL uses increasing sampling compute to move from expected-reward training toward maximum likelihood for tasks with terminal binary feedback.

papers.title: Online Compatible Reward Identification from Preference Feedback
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes preference-query requirements for identifying broadly accurate compatible rewards and develops an efficient query-basis algorithm.

papers.title: PAWS: Preference Learning with Advantage-Weighted Segments
papers.tldr: PAWS improves preference-based policy learning by keeping utility training and policy updates aligned at the segment level.

papers.title: Position: Deployed Reinforcement Learning should be Continual
papers.tldr: The authors argue that deployed reward-guided agents unable to achieve optimality should keep learning as conditions change.

papers.title: ProRL: Effective Reinforcement Learning for Proactive Recommendation via Rectified Policy Gradient Estimation
papers.tldr: ProRL corrects path-length bias and reduces gradient variance to improve reinforcement learning for proactive recommendation.

papers.title: Recovering Hidden Reward in Diffusion-Based Policies
papers.tldr: EnergyFlow structures diffusion action models to recover rewards under maximum-entropy optimality while improving imitation and downstream reinforcement learning.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning with Pairwise Preferences in Long-Term Decision Problems
papers.tldr: Markov decision contests enable long-horizon learning from pairwise preferences with optimal stationary-policy guarantees and a convergent iterative algorithm.

papers.title: Reward Learning through Ranking Mean Squared Error
papers.tldr: R4 learns rewards from ordered human ratings using a ranking loss with formal guarantees and competitive robotic-benchmark performance.

papers.title: SHAP-Guided Kernel Actor-Critic for Explainable Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: RSA2C uses SHAP-derived state-feature importance to guide kernel actor–critic learning, with convergence analysis and continuous-control evaluations.

papers.title: The Axiomatic Value of Regularization in AI Alignment from Human Preferences
papers.tldr: Regularization improves the social choice properties of von Neumann winner RLHF methods, while regularized Borda-based objectives still fail key axioms.

papers.title: Trust Region Inverse Reinforcement Learning: Explicit Dual Ascent using Local Policy Updates
papers.tldr: TRIRL uses carefully reduced reward updates and local policy searches to obtain monotonic inverse-reinforcement-learning improvement without a full RL solve each iteration.

papers.title: Understanding the Performance Gap in Preference Learning: A Dichotomy of RLHF and DPO
papers.tldr: The analysis shows that RLHF, DPO, and online DPO have different advantages depending on model misspecification and finite-sample conditions.
